title: Typed CSV input and round-trip data contracts
outcome: Parse and export bounded CSV data using explicit types and missingness rules rather than accidental inference.

exercises.title: Preserve a textual ID
exercises.hint: Identity is not necessarily a measurement.
exercises.answer: Numeric-looking keys can lose meaning when inference converts them to integers.

exercises.title: Declare missingness
exercises.task: Parse the authored NA amount marker.
exercises.answer: A missing marker should not silently become a valid numeric zero.

exercises.title: Reject a wrong type
exercises.task: Parse 1.5 as a strict integer field.
exercises.expected: The parser raises its typed-input error.
exercises.hint: A decimal value violates this declared schema.
exercises.answer: Changing the schema or using a repair policy requires an explicit decision.

exercises.title: Retain quoted content
exercises.task: Round-trip a string containing a comma or quotation marks.
exercises.hint: Use the CSV writer instead of hand-concatenating fields.
exercises.answer: Correct quoting preserves structure without promising byte-identical formatting to every original file.

exercises.title: Handle buffer position
exercises.task: Write to an IOBuffer and then read its contents.
exercises.expected: Reset or take the bytes explicitly.
exercises.answer: An empty read after a write can reflect the current position rather than missing source data.

exercises.title: Separate parsing and meaning
exercises.task: A file parses successfully but has duplicate entity IDs.
exercises.expected: The relational data contract still needs validation.
exercises.hint: Parsing proves only part of the input boundary.
exercises.answer: Types and delimiters do not establish grain, units or scientific validity.
